# zag workbench

> A standards-native, Zig-native workbench where people and agents do engineering work in one recorded workspace.

Everything that happens becomes a typed event in a hash-chained log. Agents propose typed tool requests; a local policy engine decides them. Terminology, metadata, accessibility, data quality and AI governance are enforced by the build, not described in a document.

## Docs

- [README](/README.md): What the workbench is and how to build it
- [Architecture](/docs/architecture.md): The event graph, the block model and the standards control plane
- [Standards conformance](/docs/standards-conformance.md): Which standards apply, how each is checked, and what is not established
- [Plain language](/docs/plain-language.md): How ISO 24495 is applied to product text, and what the checker cannot decide
- [Glossary](/docs/glossary.md): The registered concepts and their definitions

## Machine-readable

- [Workspace vocabulary (SKOS)](/vocab/workspace.ttl): Concepts, definitions and relations
- [Event schema](/schemas/workspace-event.schema.json): JSON Schema for the typed event stream
- [Tool request schema](/schemas/tool-request.schema.json): What an agent may ask for
- [Daemon interface](/schemas/openapi.json): OpenAPI description of the workspace daemon
- [Metadata registry](/schemas/metadata-registry.json): Registered field names and their value domains

## Optional

- [Decision records](/docs/adr/): Why the architecture is the way it is
- [Risk register](/docs/risk-register.md): What could go wrong and what is done about it
